result.summary: Do not ship yet: reset tokens leak into web responses, and file-creation failures return 500 instead of preserving recovery.

findings.title: Reset tokens leak through the web log viewer
findings.body: The warning is sent to every configured logging sink. triggarr/logging.py:71-84 stores its unredacted token in log_buffer; routes.py:1083-1093 then renders it through partials/log_viewer.html:80. Reproduction confirmed the minted token appears in the HTTP response. Production authentication restricts this to authenticated clients, but those clients need no access to the intended operator-only logs or config volume. This is newly introduced secret exposure, not a demonstrated unauthenticated takeover.
findings.recommendation: Mark recovery log records as operator-only and exclude them from the web buffer while retaining stderr output. Test that dashboard and log-viewer responses never contain the token.

findings.title: Temporary-file creation errors escape the non-fatal handler
findings.body: tempfile.mkstemp executes before the try block. A read-only config volume, permission failure, or full disk therefore propagates through run_in_executor and returns HTTP 500 after the token and rate-limit timestamp have already been committed. Injecting PermissionError reproduced this response. The operator receives no recovery confirmation despite the token having been logged; immediate retries return 429.
findings.recommendation: Move temporary-file creation inside the guarded block, initialize cleanup state safely, and verify creation failures still return the neutral confirmation.

next_steps: Separate operator-only token logging from web-visible logs.
Handle temporary-file creation failures and add focused regression tests.
